skills.name: Transmission of heat and electricity by conduction

note.text:
Conduction is the transfer of heat (or electricity) through a material without the material itself moving.
Heat conduction: the particles at the hot end vibrate faster and pass the energy to their neighbours. Metals conduct heat best, because they also have free electrons that carry energy.
Experiment: fix drops of wax along rods of copper, aluminium, iron and glass and heat one end of each: the wax melts furthest along the copper rod first.
Order (best conductor first): copper, aluminium, iron, … glass, wood, plastic.
Electrical conduction: a current flows only in a closed circuit made of conductors. In metals, electrons carry the current. Put a material in a circuit with a cell and a bulb: if the bulb lights, the material conducts.

worked_example.problem: Ngwa leaves {m} in a pot of hot soup. After a while the handle is hot. Explain.
steps: The spoon touches the hot soup at one end.
Its particles there vibrate faster and pass the energy along the spoon: conduction.
Steel is a metal, a good conductor, so the handle soon gets hot.
worked_example.answer: Heat is conducted along the metal spoon to the handle.

cards.idea: In conduction, energy passes from particle to particle; the material does not move.
example: The handle of a metal spoon in hot tea gets hot.
The spoon stays where it is.

cards.idea: Metals conduct heat best; copper is better than aluminium, which is better than iron.
example: Wax melts first along the copper rod.

cards.idea: Electric current flows only in a closed circuit of conductors.
example: A bulb lights when a metal key closes the circuit.
A plastic pen leaves the bulb off.

pick.r: heat passing through a material from particle to particle
w: a material moving to carry heat
pick.y: Energy passes between particles; the material stays still.

pick.q: Why do metals conduct heat well?
pick.r: They have free electrons that carry energy.
pick.y: Free electrons carry energy quickly through a metal.

questions.prompt: Put these materials in order, best conductor of heat first.

pick.q: The bulb lights. What does this show?
e: A flat cell would not light the bulb.
A broken bulb would not light.
pick.y: The circuit is closed through a conductor.

pick.q: Which of these would light the bulb?
The bulb stays off with a glass rod. What does this show?
pick.y: No current flows through an insulator.

questions.prompt: A material is placed in a circuit with a cell and a bulb. {X.q}

pick.q: On which rod does the wax melt furthest first?
e: Iron conducts, but less well than copper.
pick.y: Copper is the best conductor of the four.

pick.q: What must be kept the same for a fair test?
pick.r: the length and thickness of the rods and the heat given
w: only the colour of the rods
e: A fair test keeps other variables the same.
The material is what we change.

pick.q: On which rod does the wax hardly melt?
e: Iron is a metal and conducts.
pick.y: Glass is a poor conductor of heat.

questions.prompt: Drops of wax are stuck along rods of different materials, and one end of each rod is heated. {X.q}

right.text: Copper conducts heat better than iron.
Wood is a poor conductor of heat.
In conduction the material does not move.

wrong.text: In conduction the hot material flows to the cold place.
wrong.explain: That is convection; in conduction the material stays still.

wrong.text: Glass conducts heat better than copper.
wrong.explain: Copper is a far better conductor.

wrong.text: A bulb lights in an open circuit.
wrong.explain: Current flows only in a closed circuit.
